newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bogota Mime artists talk about pay delay.
newsitem.headline: Bogota Mime artists talk about pay delay.

text.p: Mime artists who work for city hall to promote civic values in Bogota are breaking their silence over two months of wages tangled in red tape.

Seventy mime artists are employed to shame pedestrians and motorists silently into becoming more responsible. But the street performers have not been paid for their morality sketches since September and about 30 staged a protest at a city museum on Wednesday to highlight the cash crisis.
"We've come to throw coins in the museum well so that our wishes come true. Somebody is juggling the books and we want the wages we're owed," actor Carlos Gomez told the El Espectador newspaper.

City hall official Paul Blomberg, head of the programme entitled "Polis In Action," said on Thursday he did not know how much each mime artist was owed but the six-month pilot project cost $100,000. He said the open-air actors had not been paid because of "gaps in the paperwork" but that they would receive their back pay in the next few days.
